Commentary.Commentary: We are all set to start. Tim Southee to start the attack for New Zealand. Its Mahmudul Hasan Joy along with Zakir Hasan to open the batting for Bangladesh. Lets play!
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Bangladesh on the other hand were brilliant with the ball yesterday. Shoriful Islam set the tone upfront with the new ball bowling a brilliant spell to the openers. Followed him were the spinners in Taijul Islam who grabbed 4 wickets picking up the big wicket of Kane Williamson whom he dropped earlier in the day. Mehidy Hasan along with Nayeem Hasan picked 1 wicket each to restrict the Kiwis to 266 at the end of the day. Mominul Haque picked up his best figures in test cricket grabbing 3 wickets for his team. New Zealand are bowled out for 317 and now it will be Bangladesh with the bat again to play their second innings. The wicket getting better for the spinners day after day and it will be a treat to see how the Bangladeshi batters take the Kiwi bowlers on.

New Zealand started their batting on a roller coaster with both the openers getting decent starts but the getting out in quick succession. Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls then stitched up a 54-run partnership before Henry Nicholls fell before Shoriful Islam on 19. Williamson then joined Daryl Mitchell and got another 66-run partnership.  After Daryl Mitchell’s wicket, Williamson got another 78-run partnership with Glenn Phillips. It was not easy but it was an outstanding inning by the former New Zealand skipper Kane Williamson who went on to score his 29th Test century scoring 104 off 205 balls with 11 beautiful boundaries taking the Kiwis to a total of 266 with the loss of 8 wickets at the end of the second day. Williamson got out with 8 overs left at the end of the day. It was then the pair of Tim Southee and Kyle Jamieson to put up another 50-run partnership and take the team to a lead of 7 runs in the first innings.

That sums up the New Zealand innings as they are bowled out for 317 by Bangladesh. New Zealand now have a lead of 7 runs in the first innings and the game is brilliantly poised for the second innings to come.

He floats this one up, full and on middle, Tim Southee backs away a bit and tries to whip it across the line but plays all around it and misses as the ball goes through to shatter the stumps. New Zealand have been bowled out for 317!

Taijul Islam's four-wicket haul, including the prized scalp of Kane Williamson, showcased the effectiveness of the spinners on a wicket that is gradually favoring turn. As the teams retire for the day, Bangladesh holds the advantage with the opportunity to secure a first-innings lead. The wicket's increasing favorability for spin bowlers hints at a challenging task for the Kiwi batsmen on the morrow, setting the stage for an absorbing continuation of this Test match.

The New Zealand innings unfolded as a roller coaster, with openers making promising starts but succumbing to quick wickets. Kane Williamson, the former captain, showcased his class with a masterful innings, anchoring partnerships with Henry Nicholls, Daryl Mitchell, and Glenn Phillips. Williamson's resilience was on full display as he reached his 29th Test century, scoring 104 off 205 balls with 11 boundaries. Despite his valiant efforts, New Zealand ended the day with 8 wickets down, leaving the lower order to navigate the remaining overs. As Kyle Jamieson and skipper Tim Southee prepare to resume batting on the third day, the match is delicately poised with Bangladesh aiming to capitalize on their lead.

The culmination of the second day's play in the 1st Test between New Zealand and Bangladesh has set the stage for an intriguing contest between bat and ball. The hosts, Bangladesh, began the day with their overnight score of 310, and New Zealand swiftly wrapped up the innings by dismissing the last Bangladeshi batter in the first ball of the day. The Kiwis then embarked on their first innings, finishing the day at 266 for the loss of 8 wickets, trailing Bangladesh by 44 runs.

As for Bangladesh, they had their tails up ever since getting rid of Daryl Mitchell and things would have been pretty different had Taijul Islam managed to complete the straight forward catch of Kane Williamson. At the start of the second session, the spinners toiled hard but it was Taijul Islam who gave them the first breakthrough of the post-lunch session. Taijul Islam was then rewarded for his persistence as he foxed the dangerous-looking Daryl Mitchell. That said, they missed a trick early on when Daryl Mitchell had edged one behind to Nurul Hasan but neither of the Bangladesh players were interested in going for the review. SESSION SUMMARY - 90 runs, 28 overs and 2 wickets. Another absorbing session of Test cricket comes to an end. Every ball was an event in the last few overs before the break and as it stands, New Zealand trail by 142 runs. With the fall of two openers in the first session, New Zealand needed Kane Williamson and Henry Nicholls to start well in the second session. They did a decent job of keeping the Bangladesh spinners at bay until Nicholls edged one behind off the left-arm pacer Shoriful Islam. Having survived an early scare in the innings, Daryl Mitchell continued his attacking intent and did not allow the Bangladesh spinners to settle. Kane Williamson held firm at the other end and thanks to his partnership with Mitchell, the runs began to flow at a good nick. A lapse in concentration resulted in Mitchell's departure which left New Zealand with a tricky phase before Tea. Kane Williamson and Tom Blundell joined hands to ensure they saw through that phase and there was no further damage.
